page: Microsoft Azure D48alds_v6 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. It features 48 vCPUs across 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The system is configured with 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 2835 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is premium storage capable under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark results place this server in the top 25% for both single-core and multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng, as well as Geekbench multi-core and Passmark CPU tests. Memory performance is strong for cached small-block reads at 3648.29 GB/sec, though large-block uncached read and write operations fall into the average tier. Cryptographic and database operations perform strongly, with Redis SET operations reaching 66.39 million operations per second. For machine learning workloads, the server achieves top-tier text generation speeds of 339.07 tokens per second on small 135M models, but performance drops to the bottom 10% for text generation on large 70B models.

Given the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this server represents a compute-optimized hardware profile with a high-density local NVMe storage tradeoff. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring high raw compute power and fast local scratch space rather than massive memory footprints. Optimal workloads include software compilation, database operations, high-throughput web serving, and small-scale model inference.
description: The Microsoft Azure D48alds_v6 is a compute-optimized server featuring a dedicated 48-vCPU AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Configured with 96.0 GB of RAM and a bundled 2835 GB NVMe SSD, this virtual machine operates under Microsoft Hyper-V. It delivers strong CPU and database performance, ranking in the top 25% for multi-core stress-ng and Passmark benchmarks, alongside high-throughput Redis operations. However, its 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio represents a tradeoff for memory-intensive applications, and text generation performance for large 70B models is poor. This server is highly suited for compute-heavy workloads, software compilation, database operations, and small-scale machine learning inference.
